{{Short description|Theorem in field theory}}
In [[field theory (mathematics)|field theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''isomorphism extension theorem''' is an important [[theorem]] regarding the extension of a [[field (mathematics)|field]] [[isomorphism]] to a larger field.

== Isomorphism extension theorem ==
The theorem states that given any field <math>F</math>, an [[algebraic extension]] field <math>E</math> of <math>F</math> and an isomorphism <math>\phi</math> mapping <math>F</math> [[onto]] a field <math>F'</math> then <math>\phi</math> can be extended to an isomorphism <math>\tau</math> mapping <math>E</math> onto an algebraic extension <math>E'</math> of <math>F'</math> (a [[Field extension|subfield]] of the [[algebraic closure]] of <math>F'</math>).

The proof of the isomorphism extension theorem in its most general setting, i.e. for the case of a field extension of infinite degree, depends on [[Zorn's lemma]].

==References==
* [[Donald John Lewis|D.J. Lewis]], ''Introduction to algebra'', [[Harper & Row]], 1965, Chap.IV.12, p.193.
